quests.instruction: Choose the three main events, in order, and leave out the vivid detail that changes nothing.
quests.story: Tariq's hiking group planned to reach the summit by noon, but a fallen tree blocked the main path. A deer crossed the trail just before the ridge. The leader checked the map and found a longer route around the ridge, and the group reached the summit at two.
options: The leader found a longer route around the ridge on the map.
The group reached the summit at two.
A fallen tree blocked the hikers' main path.
A deer crossed the trail just before the ridge.
quests.hint: Ask whether removing an event would change what happens next.
quests.explanation: The deer is memorable but the group's route and arrival time are exactly the same without it. The main line is the blocked path, the detour, and the late summit.
storyKeyEvents: A fallen tree blocked the hikers' main path.
The leader found a longer route around the ridge on the map.
The group reached the summit at two.

quests.instruction: Which three events would a short summary of the lessons keep?
quests.story: Jana's eight-year-old brother was afraid to put his face in the water. The instructor let him practise blowing bubbles at the pool's edge while holding her hand. The lights above the pool flickered briefly during the second lesson. By the end of the fourth lesson he swam a full length with his face down.
options: By the fourth lesson he swam a full length with his face down.
The lights above the pool flickered during the second lesson.
Jana's brother was afraid to put his face in the water.
The instructor let him practise blowing bubbles at the pool's edge.
quests.hint: Some events belong to the building, not to the boy's progress.
quests.explanation: The flickering lights happened around him but had no effect on his fear. His progress runs from the fear, to the bubble practice, to the full length.
storyKeyEvents: Jana's brother was afraid to put his face in the water.
The instructor let him practise blowing bubbles at the pool's edge.
By the fourth lesson he swam a full length with his face down.

quests.instruction: Arrange the three main events that a summary of Ruben's season would need.
quests.story: Ruben joined the chess club but lost his first six matches. He preferred playing with the black pieces, which he said felt calmer. A club member showed him how to review each game afterwards, and he began writing down his mistakes. In the spring tournament he won three matches in a row.
options: Ruben preferred playing with the black pieces, which he said felt calmer.
Ruben lost his first six matches at the chess club.
A club member showed Ruben how to review games, and he began writing down his mistakes.
Ruben won three matches in a row in the spring tournament.
quests.hint: A personal taste can be true without explaining the outcome.
quests.explanation: His liking for black pieces doesn't explain why he began winning. The turn comes from learning to review his games, which sits between the losses and the winning streak.
storyKeyEvents: Ruben lost his first six matches at the chess club.
A club member showed Ruben how to review games, and he began writing down his mistakes.
Ruben won three matches in a row in the spring tournament.

quests.instruction: Pick the three events a short summary of this seminar problem must keep.
quests.story: Only nine of the twenty-four students were attending Ms. Okafor's university seminar. She asked the class why, and several said the 8 a.m. start clashed with the bus timetable. The module cost £180 per student, paid at the start of term. She moved the seminar to 10 a.m., and attendance rose to twenty.
options: Ms. Okafor moved the seminar to 10 a.m. and attendance rose to twenty.
The module cost £180 per student, paid at the start of term.
Students said the 8 a.m. start clashed with the bus timetable.
Only nine of the twenty-four students were attending the seminar.
quests.hint: A number is not automatically an important number. Does this one explain anything?
quests.explanation: The fee is a precise figure, but it plays no part in low attendance or the fix. The summary needs the poor turnout, the bus clash, and the later start.
storyKeyEvents: Only nine of the twenty-four students were attending the seminar.
Students said the 8 a.m. start clashed with the bus timetable.
Ms. Okafor moved the seminar to 10 a.m. and attendance rose to twenty.

quests.instruction: Choose the three main events, in order.
quests.story: Lena viewed a flat that was cheaper than the others on her list, but she noticed damp patches in the bedroom. In the hallway, another couple was measuring the kitchen with a tape while Lena looked around. She asked the agent whether the damp would be treated, and the agent admitted it had not been. Lena decided not to apply and kept looking.
options: Another couple was measuring the kitchen with a tape while Lena looked around.
The agent admitted the damp had not been treated.
Lena noticed damp patches in the flat's bedroom.
Lena decided not to apply and kept looking.
quests.hint: Two viewings are happening at once. Only one of them drives Lena's decision.
quests.explanation: The other couple's measuring shows the flat was popular, but it doesn't bear on Lena's choice. Her decision follows the damp and the agent's admission.
storyKeyEvents: Lena noticed damp patches in the flat's bedroom.
The agent admitted the damp had not been treated.
Lena decided not to apply and kept looking.

quests.instruction: Which three events does a short summary need?
quests.story: Three colleagues shared a car to work, but Priya, who drove, often arrived late after collecting the others. Priya remarked that she had never liked driving on the motorway, even on quiet days. Neil suggested they take turns driving and follow a fixed pick-up order. With the new rota, the group arrived on time every day.
options: Priya remarked that she had never liked driving on the motorway, even on quiet days.
With the new rota, the group arrived on time every day.
Neil suggested taking turns driving with a fixed pick-up order.
Priya, who drove, often arrived late after collecting the others.
quests.hint: Comments in passing rarely explain what happened afterwards.
quests.explanation: Priya's remark about the motorway doesn't connect to the lateness or the rota. The line the summary follows is lateness, the rota idea, and on-time arrivals.
storyKeyEvents: Priya, who drove, often arrived late after collecting the others.
Neil suggested taking turns driving with a fixed pick-up order.
With the new rota, the group arrived on time every day.

quests.instruction: Arrange the three events that a summary of Marek's morning must keep.
quests.story: Marek's card was rejected by the ticket machine at the station. An assistant noticed the machine's card reader was faulty and sold him a ticket at the counter. Marek offered him a biscuit from his bag as thanks, which the assistant politely declined. Marek caught the 8:40 with two minutes to spare.
options: The ticket machine rejected Marek's card.
Marek offered the assistant a biscuit as thanks.
An assistant noticed the reader was faulty and sold him a ticket at the counter.
Marek caught the 8:40 with two minutes to spare.
quests.hint: A kind gesture can be lovely and still not be needed to follow the sequence.
quests.explanation: The biscuit was declined and had no effect on his travel. His morning depends on the rejected card, the counter sale, and catching the train.
storyKeyEvents: The ticket machine rejected Marek's card.
An assistant noticed the reader was faulty and sold him a ticket at the counter.
Marek caught the 8:40 with two minutes to spare.

quests.instruction: Pick the three events that a summary of the client's decision would use.
quests.story: Abena's team presented their project plan to a client on Friday. The client asked for a cheaper option, so the team cut the second phase and resubmitted the plan by Monday. Two years earlier the same client had walked away from a larger proposal. On Tuesday the client signed the reduced plan.
options: The same client had walked away from a larger proposal two years earlier.
The team cut the second phase and resubmitted the plan by Monday.
The client signed the reduced plan on Tuesday.
The client asked Abena's team for a cheaper option.
quests.hint: Past history can add flavour without being part of this week's sequence.
quests.explanation: The earlier walk-away is a separate episode from two years before and doesn't change what happens this week. The summary is the request, the cut-down plan, and the signature.
storyKeyEvents: The client asked Abena's team for a cheaper option.
The team cut the second phase and resubmitted the plan by Monday.
The client signed the reduced plan on Tuesday.

quests.instruction: Which three events would a summary of the language exchange keep?
quests.story: Hye-jin arranged a language exchange with a student, Diego, to practise English while teaching him Korean. They met in the campus café every Thursday and swapped twenty minutes each way. On the first day she went to the wrong café and found the right one within five minutes. After six weeks she could hold a ten-minute conversation in English.
options: They met in the campus café every Thursday and swapped twenty minutes each way.
Hye-jin arranged a language exchange with Diego.
After six weeks Hye-jin could hold a ten-minute conversation in English.
On the first day Hye-jin went to the wrong café and found the right one within five minutes.
quests.hint: A small slip that is fixed within minutes seldom belongs in a summary.
quests.explanation: Going to the wrong café cost her five minutes once and left no mark on the arrangement. The summary covers the set-up, the weekly routine, and the result.
storyKeyEvents: Hye-jin arranged a language exchange with Diego.
They met in the campus café every Thursday and swapped twenty minutes each way.
After six weeks Hye-jin could hold a ten-minute conversation in English.

quests.instruction: Choose the three main events, in order.
quests.story: Selam attended the university job fair hoping to find an internship in logistics. It was busier than the year before, with thirty stalls. At one stall a manager asked her to send her CV that evening and follow up on Monday. On Monday the manager invited her to an interview, and two weeks later she was offered a summer placement.
options: Selam was invited to an interview and later offered a summer placement.
Selam went to the job fair hoping to find a logistics internship.
The fair was busier than the year before, with thirty stalls.
A manager at one stall asked her to send her CV and follow up on Monday.
quests.hint: Comparisons with earlier years describe the setting, not the plot.
quests.explanation: How busy the fair was compared with last year tells us nothing about how Selam got her placement. The summary needs her goal, the manager's request, and the offer.
storyKeyEvents: Selam went to the job fair hoping to find a logistics internship.
A manager at one stall asked her to send her CV and follow up on Monday.
Selam was invited to an interview and later offered a summer placement.

quests.instruction: Which three events would a summary need to keep?
quests.story: Mr. Alvarez went to the pharmacy to collect a prescription, but the pharmacist said the doctor had sent it to a different branch. A toddler in the queue dropped an ice cream and started crying. The pharmacist phoned the other branch and arranged a transfer, which took twenty minutes. Mr. Alvarez then collected his medicine.
options: A toddler in the queue dropped an ice cream and started crying.
Mr. Alvarez collected his medicine.
The pharmacist phoned the other branch and arranged a transfer.
The pharmacist said the prescription had been sent to a different branch.
quests.hint: An eye-catching moment is not the same as an important one.
quests.explanation: The crying toddler catches attention, but nothing about the prescription depends on it. The summary follows the misdirected prescription, the transfer, and the collection.
storyKeyEvents: The pharmacist said the prescription had been sent to a different branch.
The pharmacist phoned the other branch and arranged a transfer.
Mr. Alvarez collected his medicine.

quests.instruction: Arrange the three main events, ignoring the background detail.
quests.story: Kamal had never performed in public, but a friend signed him up for the Wednesday open-mic night at a café. He played two songs on his guitar, and the café owner recorded the second one. Rain began to fall outside halfway through the evening. The owner posted the recording, and it reached two thousand views in a week.
options: A friend signed Kamal up for the open-mic night.
The posted recording reached two thousand views in a week.
Rain began to fall outside halfway through the evening.
The café owner recorded Kamal's second song.
quests.hint: Weather can be part of a scene without being part of the story.
quests.explanation: The rain was only the backdrop and didn't change what Kamal or the owner did. The story turns on the sign-up, the recording, and its success online.
storyKeyEvents: A friend signed Kamal up for the open-mic night.
The café owner recorded Kamal's second song.
The posted recording reached two thousand views in a week.

quests.instruction: Pick the three events a summary of the sale would keep.
quests.story: Fiona listed her old sofa on an online marketplace for £120. The first buyer who messaged never replied after Fiona asked about pickup. Fiona liked to arrange pickups in the afternoon. A second buyer collected the sofa on Saturday and paid £110 after negotiating.
options: Fiona liked to arrange pickups in the afternoon.
The first buyer never replied after Fiona asked about pickup.
Fiona listed her old sofa for £120.
A second buyer collected the sofa and paid £110.
quests.hint: Habits and tastes describe a person, but do they move this sale forward?
quests.explanation: Her preference for afternoons is a personal habit that doesn't alter who bought the sofa or for how much. The summary follows the listing, the silent buyer, and the sale.
storyKeyEvents: Fiona listed her old sofa for £120.
The first buyer never replied after Fiona asked about pickup.
A second buyer collected the sofa and paid £110.

quests.instruction: Which three events would a summary of the contest need to keep?
quests.story: Amina entered a local photography contest with a picture of the harbour at dawn. The entry fee was £8, payable online. The judges chose her photo as one of ten finalists, and it was displayed in the town library for a month. Visitors voted, and hers won the public prize.
options: The entry fee was £8, payable online.
Amina entered a picture of the harbour at dawn.
Visitors voted and her photo won the public prize.
The judges chose her photo as a finalist and it was displayed in the library.
quests.hint: Ask whether a figure helps you understand what happened, or just adds precision.
quests.explanation: The fee is a real figure, but it doesn't affect how the photo fares. The result follows from the entry, the finalist display, and the public vote.
storyKeyEvents: Amina entered a picture of the harbour at dawn.
The judges chose her photo as a finalist and it was displayed in the library.
Visitors voted and her photo won the public prize.

quests.instruction: Arrange the three main events, in order.
quests.story: Petra's moving van was booked for nine, but it arrived at eleven because of a breakdown on an earlier job. A neighbour carried her own boxes down the stairs while the movers worked. The movers loaded everything quickly, and the flat was empty by one. Petra handed over the keys at two.
options: Petra handed over the keys at two.
The moving van arrived two hours late, at eleven.
The movers loaded everything and the flat was empty by one.
A neighbour carried her own boxes down the stairs.
quests.hint: Someone else's activity nearby isn't automatically part of your character's day.
quests.explanation: The neighbour's boxes are unrelated to Petra's move. Her day runs from the late van, to the emptied flat, to handing back the keys.
storyKeyEvents: The moving van arrived two hours late, at eleven.
The movers loaded everything and the flat was empty by one.
Petra handed over the keys at two.

quests.instruction: Choose the three events that carry Jamila's progress.
quests.story: Jamila's tutoring session on fractions went nowhere until the tutor drew a circle cut into eight slices. When Jamila coloured three slices, she suddenly saw why three eighths is smaller than half. Her mother said the tutor was expensive for a single hour. By the end of the hour Jamila solved six similar problems on her own.
options: Jamila solved six similar problems on her own by the end of the hour.
Jamila's mother said the tutor was expensive for a single hour.
The tutor drew a circle in eight slices and Jamila coloured three.
Jamila's session on fractions went nowhere at first.
quests.hint: Someone's opinion about the situation isn't the same as something happening in it.
quests.explanation: The mother's comment concerns cost, not learning, and Jamila's progress doesn't depend on it. The progress runs from confusion, to the drawing, to solving problems alone.
storyKeyEvents: Jamila's session on fractions went nowhere at first.
The tutor drew a circle in eight slices and Jamila coloured three.
Jamila solved six similar problems on her own by the end of the hour.

quests.instruction: Choose the three main events, in order.
quests.story: Lucas arrived at the conference to find his name missing from the registration list. He held the door open for two other attendees walking in behind him. A volunteer checked the booking email on his phone and found that the registration had been made under his old surname. She corrected the list and gave him a badge, and he reached the first talk with five minutes to spare.
options: She corrected the list and Lucas reached the first talk with five minutes to spare.
Lucas held the door open for two other attendees walking in behind him.
Lucas found his name missing from the registration list.
A volunteer found the registration had been made under his old surname.
quests.hint: Courtesy shows character, but does it help solve the registration problem?
quests.explanation: Holding the door is polite but has no connection to the missing name. The problem is found, explained by the old surname, and solved by the corrected list.
storyKeyEvents: Lucas found his name missing from the registration list.
A volunteer found the registration had been made under his old surname.
She corrected the list and Lucas reached the first talk with five minutes to spare.

quests.instruction: Pick the three events that make up the story of the glass bank.
quests.story: The residents of Maple Court wanted to recycle more, but the general bins were full by Wednesday. Ruth had once seen a glass bank next to the market in her home town. She counted the bins and noticed that glass took up most of the space, so she asked the council for a separate glass bank. The council installed one in March, and the general bins stayed half empty afterwards.
options: The council installed a glass bank and the general bins stayed half empty.
Ruth asked the council for a separate glass bank after noticing glass filled most of the space.
The general bins at Maple Court were full by Wednesday.
Ruth had once seen a glass bank next to the market in her home town.
quests.hint: An earlier memory can hint at where an idea came from without being a step in the chain.
quests.explanation: Seeing a glass bank elsewhere is an aside that doesn't add a step. Ruth's action runs from the full bins, to counting and asking, to the installation and the result.
storyKeyEvents: The general bins at Maple Court were full by Wednesday.
Ruth asked the council for a separate glass bank after noticing glass filled most of the space.
The council installed a glass bank and the general bins stayed half empty.

quests.instruction: Which three events would a short summary of the launch keep?
quests.story: Giulia's team launched their app on Monday morning. In the first hour the login page briefly showed an error, which the developer fixed in ten minutes. By noon two thousand people had downloaded the app. By Friday the team had reached five thousand downloads.
options: Giulia's team launched their app on Monday morning.
Two thousand people had downloaded the app by noon.
The login page briefly showed an error that the developer fixed in ten minutes.
The team reached five thousand downloads by Friday.
quests.hint: A problem fixed within minutes may not deserve a place in a summary.
quests.explanation: The login glitch was solved quickly and never affected the download totals. What matters is the launch, the strong first morning, and the week's total.
storyKeyEvents: Giulia's team launched their app on Monday morning.
Two thousand people had downloaded the app by noon.
The team reached five thousand downloads by Friday.

quests.instruction: Choose the three events that tell the story of the route change.
quests.story: The city changed the number 14 bus route to avoid roadworks on Mill Street. Commuters who used the old stop found it empty on Monday and missed their buses. The new route was longer than people had expected, adding about ten minutes. After complaints, the city put temporary signs at the old stop pointing to the new one, and missed buses fell within days.
options: The city changed the number 14 route to avoid roadworks on Mill Street.
The new route was longer than people had expected, adding about ten minutes.
The city put signs at the old stop and missed buses fell within days.
Commuters found the old stop empty on Monday and missed their buses.
quests.hint: Look for a detail that measures reality against expectations rather than adding an event.
quests.explanation: The route's length compared with expectations is an observation that doesn't change the chain. The story goes from the change, to missed buses, to the signs.
storyKeyEvents: The city changed the number 14 route to avoid roadworks on Mill Street.
Commuters found the old stop empty on Monday and missed their buses.
The city put signs at the old stop and missed buses fell within days.

quests.instruction: Arrange the three main events of Deepak's first day.
quests.story: On Deepak's first day at the design agency, his manager introduced him to the team and gave him a small task: redrawing an old logo. A pigeon flew in through an open window and circled the studio for a minute before leaving. Deepak finished the logo by the afternoon, and the manager asked him to present it at Friday's meeting.
options: A pigeon flew into the studio through an open window.
The manager asked him to present the logo at Friday's meeting.
The manager introduced Deepak to the team and gave him a logo to redraw.
Deepak finished the logo by the afternoon.
quests.hint: A funny interruption may be the most memorable line and still not belong.
quests.explanation: The pigeon didn't affect Deepak's task in any way. His day moves from the assignment, to finishing it, to the invitation to present.
storyKeyEvents: The manager introduced Deepak to the team and gave him a logo to redraw.
Deepak finished the logo by the afternoon.
The manager asked him to present the logo at Friday's meeting.

quests.instruction: Which three events belong in a summary of Nora's pottery class?
quests.story: Nora joined a beginner pottery class, but her first bowls kept collapsing on the wheel. The kiln hummed all afternoon while the students worked. The teacher noticed that she pressed too hard and showed her how to use a lighter touch. By the fifth week her bowls stood up, and she sold two at the class's end-of-term sale.
options: The teacher noticed she pressed too hard and showed her a lighter touch.
The kiln hummed all afternoon while the students worked.
Nora's first bowls kept collapsing on the wheel.
By the fifth week Nora's bowls stood up and she sold two at the sale.
quests.hint: Background sounds and smells set the mood, but rarely the plot.
quests.explanation: The kiln's humming describes the studio and has no bearing on why the bowls fell or stood. The summary is the collapsing bowls, the teacher's correction, and the sale.
storyKeyEvents: Nora's first bowls kept collapsing on the wheel.
The teacher noticed she pressed too hard and showed her a lighter touch.
By the fifth week Nora's bowls stood up and she sold two at the sale.

quests.instruction: Pick the three main events and put them in order.
quests.story: Ivan's delivery route had grown so long that parcels regularly arrived after six. Ivan preferred to start with the biggest parcels first. His supervisor studied the addresses and split the route in two, with a second driver taking the eastern streets. After the change, Ivan's parcels arrived before five.
options: After the change, Ivan's parcels arrived before five.
His supervisor split the route in two, with a second driver taking the eastern streets.
Ivan preferred to start with the biggest parcels first.
Ivan's route had grown so long that parcels regularly arrived after six.
quests.hint: Ask whether this preference explains the improvement.
quests.explanation: Ivan's preferred loading order was the same before and after, so it can't account for the change. The improvement follows the long route, the split, and the earlier arrivals.
storyKeyEvents: Ivan's route had grown so long that parcels regularly arrived after six.
His supervisor split the route in two, with a second driver taking the eastern streets.
After the change, Ivan's parcels arrived before five.

quests.instruction: Choose the three events that a summary of Saturday's problem would need.
quests.story: Mira's call-centre team was short-staffed on Saturdays, and customers waited an average of twelve minutes. The manager offered a small bonus for Saturday shifts, and six agents volunteered. The centre took about nine hundred calls a day. Waiting times on Saturdays fell to four minutes.
options: The manager offered a small bonus and six agents volunteered.
The call centre took about nine hundred calls a day.
Waiting times on Saturdays fell to four minutes.
The call-centre team was short-staffed on Saturdays and customers waited twelve minutes.
quests.hint: Not every figure is doing work. Which numbers describe the change?
quests.explanation: The daily call volume is background scale and isn't part of the shortage or its fix. The summary rests on the shortage, the bonus offer, and the shorter waits.
storyKeyEvents: The call-centre team was short-staffed on Saturdays and customers waited twelve minutes.
The manager offered a small bonus and six agents volunteered.
Waiting times on Saturdays fell to four minutes.

quests.instruction: Arrange the three main events of the drill.
quests.story: During the office fire drill on Tuesday, the alarm sounded at 10:30 and staff gathered in the car park. A delivery van was blocking the car park exit while people waited. The floor warden counted only forty-one of the forty-five people on her list. She found the other four still in a meeting room with headphones on.
options: The alarm sounded and staff gathered in the car park.
The warden counted only forty-one of forty-five people.
She found the other four still in a meeting room with headphones on.
A delivery van was blocking the car park exit while people waited.
quests.hint: Ask whether each event connects to the missing people or just happens nearby.
quests.explanation: The van is a separate obstacle that doesn't affect the head count. The drill is told through the alarm, the shortfall, and the discovery of the four.
storyKeyEvents: The alarm sounded and staff gathered in the car park.
The warden counted only forty-one of forty-five people.
She found the other four still in a meeting room with headphones on.

quests.instruction: Which three events would a summary of the book sale keep?
quests.story: The library's annual book sale usually raised a few hundred pounds. This year Alice suggested sorting the books by genre and adding handwritten recommendation cards. A visitor said the tables looked tidier than they had ever seen them. By closing time the sale had raised over a thousand pounds.
options: Alice suggested sorting the books by genre and adding recommendation cards.
By closing time the sale had raised over a thousand pounds.
The book sale usually raised only a few hundred pounds.
A visitor said the tables looked tidier than they had ever seen them.
quests.hint: An observer's comment describes the scene. Does it change the outcome?
quests.explanation: The visitor's compliment isn't something that changed the amount raised. The summary follows the usual total, Alice's idea, and the record result.
storyKeyEvents: The book sale usually raised only a few hundred pounds.
Alice suggested sorting the books by genre and adding recommendation cards.
By closing time the sale had raised over a thousand pounds.

quests.instruction: Pick the three main events of Omar's Saturday.
quests.story: Omar's food truck was booked for the weekend festival, but on Saturday morning its generator failed. The festival organiser lent him a spare generator from the sound stage, and he was serving by noon. Omar gave the organiser a free lunch to say thanks. He sold out of dumplings by four.
options: Omar gave the organiser a free lunch to say thanks.
The truck's generator failed on Saturday morning.
The organiser lent Omar a spare generator and he was serving by noon.
Omar sold out of dumplings by four.
quests.hint: Thanking someone is kind, but does it move the day forward?
quests.explanation: The free lunch came after the loan and didn't affect his sales. His day turns on the failed generator, the borrowed one, and the sell-out.
storyKeyEvents: The truck's generator failed on Saturday morning.
The organiser lent Omar a spare generator and he was serving by noon.
Omar sold out of dumplings by four.

quests.instruction: Which three events would a summary of the loan story keep?
quests.story: Wanjiru applied for a small business loan to open a tailoring shop. The bank asked for a business plan, so she spent two weekends writing one with help from a community adviser. She remembered a cousin who had opened a shop years ago and struggled with rent. The bank approved the loan in March, and she opened the shop in April.
options: Wanjiru spent two weekends writing the plan with a community adviser.
The bank approved the loan in March and she opened the shop in April.
Wanjiru remembered a cousin who had once struggled with rent.
The bank asked Wanjiru for a business plan.
quests.hint: A memory about someone else may colour a story without being one of its steps.
quests.explanation: The cousin's story is an aside from the past and doesn't feed into the application. The chain is the plan request, the writing, and the approval that led to the shop.
storyKeyEvents: The bank asked Wanjiru for a business plan.
Wanjiru spent two weekends writing the plan with a community adviser.
The bank approved the loan in March and she opened the shop in April.

quests.instruction: Choose the three main events, in order.
quests.story: Nadir's school orchestra had one week to rehearse a new piece for the parents' evening. The conductor split the players into small groups to practise the hardest passages and brought everyone together on Thursday. On Thursday a violinist arrived without her music and borrowed a copy within two minutes. The performance on Friday went without a single stop.
options: The conductor split the players into groups to practise the hardest passages.
The orchestra had one week to rehearse a new piece.
A violinist arrived without her music and borrowed a copy within two minutes.
The performance on Friday went without a single stop.
quests.hint: If a slip is put right almost at once, ask whether the story needs it.
quests.explanation: The missing music was solved within two minutes and left no trace on the performance. The summary is the tight deadline, the group practice, and the smooth concert.
storyKeyEvents: The orchestra had one week to rehearse a new piece.
The conductor split the players into groups to practise the hardest passages.
The performance on Friday went without a single stop.

quests.instruction: Pick the three events that best summarise the library's change.
quests.story: The city library extended its weekday evening hours after a survey showed that many workers could not visit before six. Staff worked shifts until eight, and the number of evening visitors doubled within a month. The building was quieter than staff expected on the first night. Membership applications rose by a third by the end of the year.
options: A survey showed many workers could not visit before six.
The number of evening visitors doubled within a month.
The library extended its weekday evening hours until eight.
The building was quieter than staff expected on the first night.
quests.hint: A first impression that later changed is easy to over-weight. Where does the story end up?
quests.explanation: The quiet first night is a snapshot that the later doubling overtakes. The core of the story is the survey, the longer hours, and the doubled visitors.
storyKeyEvents: A survey showed many workers could not visit before six.
The library extended its weekday evening hours until eight.
The number of evening visitors doubled within a month.
